original_test_intent: Verify that the intended BMC certificate workflow can generate a syntactically valid certificate signing request of the project-approved type, algorithm and subject profile in the selected certificate slot without exposing private key material or disturbing an active management certificate.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify BMC firmware/WebUI and certificate slot; inventory active certificate, pending CSR and key metadata without exporting secrets; define the required CSR type, key algorithm/size and distinguished-name/SAN fields; back up recoverable certificate state; open the specified WebUI page and populate only approved public fields; generate once after confirmation; export/capture the CSR, UI status and slot metadata; parse PEM/PKCS#10 structure, signature algorithm, public key and subject/SAN values; confirm only the intended pending request/key state changed; retain or remove it according to the approved final-state plan.
manual_activity: An operator approves the exact certificate slot, CSR profile and overwrite/final-state behavior and supervises the WebUI action; an agent may parse only the public CSR after authorization.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware and exact Certificates page/slot identity
Expected CSR container/type, key algorithm and size, signature algorithm and required subject/SAN/country values
Existing certificate/pending-request/key metadata plus backup, overwrite and final-state policy
Protected WebUI credentials, secure CSR storage/redaction and independent certificate-access recovery
safety_requirements: Inventory and back up recoverable certificate state before generation
Confirm whether the selected slot creates a new key or replaces an existing key/request
Never display, export, copy or log private key material or credentials
Generate exactly once with approved public fields and store the CSR securely
Stop on wrong/ambiguous slot, overwrite warning, unexpected key/certificate replacement, parser mismatch or management-access degradation
agent_execution_scope: Capture non-secret before/after slot metadata and approved WebUI field values
Generate one CSR only after explicit confirmation and preserve the public request
Parse PKCS#10 structure, public-key/signature algorithms and approved subject/extensions
Do not choose production state, export a private key, approve overwrite, regenerate on error or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Define what 'CSR type' means for this product and approve all algorithm/field constraints
Approve the exact slot, key creation/reuse/overwrite behavior and cleanup/final state
Approve secure storage, certificate backup and independent recovery
Review the parsed CSR and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The interactive WebUI method matches the source and its overwrite warning is appropriate, but country alone is not a CSR type and the request must be structurally parsed against an approved profile.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After slot/profile approval, use the BMC Certificates page to generate one request, capture only public PEM/metadata, and validate it with a trusted PKCS#10 parser such as `openssl req -in <csr> -noout -text -verify` without accessing the private key.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC Web Certificates workflow, actual CSR generation, CSR-type check and 5/5-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat the CSR profile as a field matrix and the certificate slot as mutable security state; correlate WebUI input, generated public PKCS#10 attributes and before/after slot metadata under a one-generation rule.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact cryptographic/subject oracle, slot/key lifecycle, backup, secure storage, structural verification and final-state handling.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A downloadable PEM or displayed country value does not prove the request is valid, uses the required key/signature algorithms or belongs to the intended slot; successful generation can still overwrite important state.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some BMCs generate a non-exportable private key and replace a pending CSR implicitly, so cleanup or restoration may not be possible without regenerating/reinstalling certificate material.

project_override_considerations: If 'CSR type' refers to a vendor UI selector rather than PKCS#10/algorithm semantics, engineering must name the exact selector/value and still require structural CSR validation. Private-key non-exportability is expected and must never be treated as missing evidence.
expected_evidence: Redacted before/after certificate/pending-CSR/key metadata and approved overwrite/final-state decision
Timestamped WebUI generation status and public CSR artifact hash
Secret-safe parsed PKCS#10 type, signature/public-key algorithms, subject, SAN/extensions and verify result
No-private-key audit, management-access health, recovery events and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for CSR generation and a CSR-type check. The required type is underspecified but no source fields contradict one another.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The certificate workflow is identifiable and a project CSR profile can be supplied. Approval and secure key-state handling are normal prerequisites, so the case is not intrinsically blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2236 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00018-V001: define exactly what BMC Web 'CSR type' means and approve the expected PKCS#10/container, key/signature algorithm and size, subject/DN/SAN/country fields; identify the certificate slot and whether generation creates/reuses/replaces key/request state; approve backup, overwrite, secure CSR storage/redaction, cleanup/final state and independent certificate-access recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves real BMC Web CSR generation while turning an undefined type check into a secure, slot-specific and cryptographically verifiable request lifecycle.
independent_technical_reasoning: A CSR contains public material, but generating it usually creates or selects a private key inside the BMC and can replace a pending request. That state change is the main safety boundary and cannot be inferred from a success message. The acceptance term 'type' could refer to PKCS#10 format, key algorithm, signature algorithm or a vendor UI category, so a supplied profile is necessary to avoid an arbitrary pass. Once approved, all public fields are machine-parseable; private key disclosure is neither needed nor allowed.
